questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.stem: A patient with severe kyphoscoliosis presents with increasing dyspnea consistent with a decrease in chest wall compliance. With the contraction of the external intercostal muscles during inspiration, the Golgi tendon organ (GTO) provides the central nervous system with information about which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The length of the muscle being moved

options.label: C
options.text: The blood flow to the muscle being moved

options.label: D
options.text: The tension developed by the muscle being moved

questions.answerText: The tension developed by the muscle being moved
questions.solutionHtml:
The tension developed by the muscle being moved
  • The Golgi tendon organ (GTO) is a sensory receptor located at the junction between skeletal muscle and tendon that responds to changes in muscle tension or force. When the external intercostal muscles contract during inspiration, the GTO provides information to the central nervous system about the tension or force being developed by the muscle. This information helps to regulate and coordinate the movement of the chest wall during breathing.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 133–135.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.stem: A 68-year-old patient with shortness of breath is referred for pulmonary function testing, including lung volumes, flow-volume curves, and lung compliance. Which one of the following statements best characterizes pulmonary compliance?

options.label: B
options.text: It is inversely related to the elastic recoil properties of the lung

options.label: D
options.text: It increases when there is a deficiency of surfactant

questions.answerText: It is inversely related to the elastic recoil properties of the lung
questions.solutionHtml:
It is inversely related to the elastic recoil properties of the lung

Lung compliance is an index of lung distensibility or the ease with which the lungs are expanded; thus, compliance is the inverse of elastic recoil.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.654–657.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.stem: A 48-year-old coal miner complains of shortness of breath and a productive cough. The history reveals that he has smoked 1 to 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 16-year-old. Pulmonary function studies are ordered including an esophageal balloon study to measure intrapleural pressures. Normally, intrapleural pressure is negative throughout a tidal inspiration and expiration because of which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The lungs have the tendency to recoil outward throughout a tidal breath

options.label: B
options.text: The chest wall has the tendency to recoil inward throughout a tidal breath

options.label: C
options.text: The intact pleura causes the lungs and chest wall to recoil away from each other throughout a tidal breath

options.label: D
options.text: The intact pleura causes the lungs and chest wall to recoil in the same direction throughout a tidal breath

questions.answerText: The intact pleura causes the lungs and chest wall to recoil away from each other throughout a tidal breath
questions.solutionHtml:
The intact pleura causes the lungs and chest wall to recoil away from each other throughout a tidal breath

During normal breathing, the lungs have the tendency to recoil inward, while the chest wall has the tendency to recoil outward. The space between the lungs and the chest wall is filled with pleural fluid, which creates a negative pressure in the intrapleural space. This negative pressure keeps the lungs inflated and causes the lungs and chest wall to move away from each other throughout a tidal breath.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.665–655.

questions.stem: Surfactant is made up of which of the following:
questions.solutionHtml:
Phospholipid

Surfactant is primarily composed of phospholipids, which are a type of lipid molecule that contains a hydrophilic (water-loving) head and a hydrophobic (water-fearing) tail.



Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 536.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.stem: A patient with right lower lobar pneumonia exhibits increasing respiratory distress. The patient is intubated, placed on a mechanical ventilator, and positioned on his left side. The dependent lung is lower?

options.label: A
options.text: Rate of alveolar ventilation per unit volume

questions.solutionHtml:
V/Q ratio

The dependent lung, which is the lung that is closer to the ground when the patient is positioned on his left side, is subject to a higher hydrostatic pressure and has a lower ventilation-perfusion (V/Q) ratio compared to the non-dependent lung.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.662–663.

During progressively increasing exercise, a person passes the first ventilatory threshold. Which description best characterises the change in ventilation beyond this threshold?

options.label: B
options.text: Ventilation decreases as exercise intensity rises
options.html: Ventilation decreases as exercise intensity rises

options.label: C
options.text: Ventilation becomes disproportionately high relative to oxygen consumption
options.html: Ventilation becomes disproportionately high relative to oxygen consumption

options.label: D
options.text: Ventilation falls to zero between breaths
options.html: Ventilation falls to zero between breaths

questions.answerText: Ventilation becomes disproportionately high relative to oxygen consumption
questions.solutionHtml:
At the ventilatory threshold, pulmonary ventilation begins to increase disproportionately relative to oxygen consumption. The illustration shows only the qualitative bend during increasing exercise intensity. It is not a calibrated exercise test and does not show a second respiratory-compensation threshold.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.stem: A candidate for cardiac transplantation undergoes cardiac catheterization. Hemodynamic findings include: Pulmonary Artery Pressure = 35 mmHg, Cardiac Output = 4 L/min, Left Atrial Pressure = 15 mmHg. Which of the following is his pulmonary vascular resistance?
questions.solutionHtml:
5 mmHg/L/min
  • Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) can be calculated using the following formula:
  • PVR = (PAP - LAP) / CO
  • where PAP is the pulmonary artery pressure, LAP is the left atrial pressure, and CO is the cardiac output.
  • Substituting the given values, we get:
  • PVR = (35 - 15) / 4
  • PVR = 20 / 4
  • PVR = 5 mmHg/L/min
  • Therefore, the answer is (C) 5 mmHg/L/min.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.650.

questions.topic: eGurukul · Pulmonary Ventilation - Compliance & Surface Tension
questions.solutionHtml:
Increase surface area by surfactant
  • The stability of alveoli is maintained by the presence of surfactant, which reduces surface tension within the alveoli, allowing them to remain open during expiration. Therefore, option (B) "increase surface area by surfactant" is the correct answer.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.660.
